title: Open Claim-Denial Appeals and Expired Prior Authorization Units
content:
### Training notes — Prior Authorization expiry and open appeals

**The rule.** The appeal hold-back of an expiry release of a Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization approval counts the member's appeals about a claim denial that are still open, that is filed, acknowledged or under review: where two or more are open, 2 units are held back; where exactly one is open, 1 unit is held back; where none is open, nothing is held back for appeals. The hold-back is a whole number of units, taken once from the units the ended approval left unused, and the units released are never below zero.

**Q. Which records does the count read?**
A. The member's cases in Appeals and Grievances whose subject is a claim denial. A case about another subject, such as a prior authorization denial, is not counted.

**Q. Which statuses make an appeal "open"?**
A. Filed, acknowledged and under review. A case in any other status is not open and is not counted.

**Q. Does it matter when the appeal was filed?**
A. No. The rule counts the appeals open on the day the release is booked, with no look-back window.

**Q. How many units are held back for each count?**

| Open claim-denial appeals | Units held back |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 or more | 2 |

**Q. A member has three open claim-denial appeals. Is the hold-back 3 units?**
A. No. Two or more open appeals hold back 2 units; the figure does not rise above 2.

*Hypothetical case, for illustration only:* a member has one claim-denial appeal under review, one claim-denial appeal whose status is no longer open, and one open appeal about a prior authorization denial. Only the first counts, so 1 unit is held back.
